payload.title: Filtering and Detrending with Pyleoclim
payload.description: This Jupyter notebook introduces users to filtering and detrending methods using the Pyleoclim library. It demonstrates how to load and visualize benthic foraminifera δ18O data from the LR04 benthic stack. The notebook covers various detrending techniques such as Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Savitzky-Golay, and filtering methods including Lanczos and Butterworth filters. The outputs include visualizations of the original and processed data, showcasing the effects of different signal processing techniques.

steps.description: Import necessary libraries and load the LR04 dataset using Pyleoclim. Plot the initial data to visualize the benthic foraminifera δ18O data.
steps.title: Preamble and Data Loading

steps.description: Apply Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to detrend the data. Visualize the original and detrended data using EMD.
steps.title: Detrending with EMD

steps.description: Use the Savitzky-Golay method to detrend the data. Plot the results to compare with the original data.
steps.title: Detrending with Savitzky-Golay

steps.description: Apply a Lanczos low-pass filter to the data with a cutoff scale of 80. Visualize the filtered data alongside the original data.
steps.title: Filtering with Lanczos

steps.description: Perform a wavelet transform on the original data using the WWZ method and plot the results.
steps.title: Wavelet Transform of Original Data

steps.description: Perform a wavelet transform on the Lanczos filtered data using the WWZ method and plot the results.
steps.title: Wavelet Transform of Filtered Data

steps.description: Apply a Butterworth bandpass filter to the data with cutoff scales of 10 and 80. Visualize the bandpass filtered data alongside the original data.
steps.title: Filtering with Butterworth

steps.description: Perform a wavelet transform on the Butterworth bandpass filtered data using the WWZ method and plot the results.
steps.title: Wavelet Transform of Bandpass Filtered Data
